title: Impostor Run: Swarm
premise: A lone impostor-like saboteur glides through a neon space-station arena, sweeping vents while avoiding an ever-growing swarm of patrolling crewmates.
interaction_model: Top-down pointer/touch-follow movement; the character continuously drifts toward the mouse or touch position, with button-based start and restart screens.
objective: Collect as many vent pickups as possible without touching any enemy patrol units.
progression: Runs begin with a small enemy set and one vent target. Each collected vent increases the score, respawns the next vent, and adds more enemy pressure, making survival progressively harder until collision ends the run.
theme: Sci-fi sabotage chase with impostor-inspired vent raiding inside a glowing spaceship surveillance grid.
mood: Tense, slick, neon, arcadey, and slightly mischievous.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy simple mobile-friendly arcade survival games, cursor-dodging score attacks, and Among Us-adjacent impostor aesthetics.
confidence_notes: High confidence in the core loop: collect vent targets while avoiding enemies in a single-screen arena.
High confidence in the control model because movement is directly tied to mouse and touch position.
Medium confidence in genre labeling because the presentation suggests impostor fiction, but the mechanics are closer to arcade survival collection than stealth.
High confidence that progression is endless score attack rather than level-based advancement.
recreation_prompt: Create a full-screen browser arcade game called "Impostor Run: Swarm" where the player controls a small impostor-like astronaut in a top-down neon sci-fi arena by moving the mouse or dragging on touchscreens, causing the character to smoothly drift toward the current pointer rather than snapping instantly. The goal is to survive as long as possible while collecting one glowing vent pickup at a time; each vent collected increases the score, immediately respawns another vent at a random location, and adds at least one more roaming enemy so the arena becomes steadily more dangerous. Enemies should look like colorful crewmate-style patrol units that spawn from screen edges, move on straight trajectories, bounce off the screen boundaries, and instantly end the run on contact with the player. Present the game as an endless score-attack survival challenge with a start screen, a restartable game-over screen showing vents swept, a compact HUD for the current score, and a brief tutorial hint like "Drag to Drift." Use a polished neon spaceship aesthetic with dark gradients, subtle grid lines, starfield motion, glowing UI panels, and juicy feedback including pickup/failure visual popups and layered audio for start, pickups, streak milestones, failure, and looping background music. Keep the mechanics simple, readable, responsive on mobile, and focused on evasive movement, objective collection, and escalating swarm pressure.
